newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey contractors plan to set up investment bank.
newsitem.headline: Turkey contractors plan to set up investment bank.

text.p: Turkish contractors are planning to set up an investment bank to finance construction projects, Kadir Sever, head of the Turkish Contractors' Union, said.
"We will apply to the treasury for the establishment of the bank in July," Sever told Reuters. The treasury must approve the application for the bank to be set up, according to the banking law.
"In our previous talks, I got the impression that the treasury was positive towards the idea," Sever said.
He said lack of enough support from Eximbank, the state export and import bank, and the limited availability of investment bank loans to contractors had forced them to found their own bank.
"Most of the construction companies will participate in the project. The bank will have some 10 to 20 partners and represent the sector," he said.
Sever said the union was also planning to set up investment and insurance companies to support the sector.
Three state and 10 private investment banks operate in Turkey.

Fourty-one leading Turkish contractors have undertaken 441 construction projects worth of $15.1 billion in 21 countries since late 1970s. About $12 billion worth of projects have already been completed, according to the union figures.
